slot.brief: Find minimum radius of a wire to support a given load without exceeding breaking stress; one-step stress = F/A.

stem: The breaking stress of a steel wire is $1.0 \times 10^{9}$ N m$^{-2}$. The minimum radius of the wire required to support a load of $3140$ N without breaking is (Take $\pi = 3.14$)
working:
Stress $= \dfrac{F}{A} \Rightarrow A = \dfrac{F}{\text{breaking stress}} = \dfrac{3140}{1.0\times 10^{9}} = 3.14 \times 10^{-6}$ m$^2$. For a wire, $A = \pi r^2$, so $r = \sqrt{\dfrac{A}{\pi}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{3.14 \times 10^{-6}}{3.14}} = 10^{-3}$ m $= 1.0$ mm.

Independent check: A = F/σ = 3140/(1.0 × 10⁹) = 3.14 × 10⁻⁶ m². Thus r = √(A/π) = 1.0 × 10⁻³ m = 1.0 mm.
solution:
Breaking stress, $\sigma=F/A$, so the minimum cross-sectional area is
$$A=\frac{3140}{1.0\times10^9}=3.14\times10^{-6}\text{ m}^2.$$
For a circular wire, $A=\pi r^2$, hence $r=\sqrt{A/\pi}=10^{-3}\text{ m}=1.0\text{ mm}$. (D)
